revised_comments: Mauritania has a comprehensive strategic framework specifically addressing government data exchange and interoperability. The National Strategy for Open and Interoperable Data (November 2022, MTNIMA) is a standalone strategy built around three axes: an interoperability framework among government entities, open data governance aligned with Open Government Partnership principles, and use of open data for innovation. It sits within the wider National Digital Transformation Agenda 2022-2025, whose public administration pillar makes interoperability and a national government cloud/intranet explicit objectives. Implementation is under way: a 2024 scoping study for the Ministry of Digital Transformation sets out a General Interoperability Framework and an Interoperability Hub (API gateway, identity and access management, unified data repository), and in March 2025 the government ran a national workshop, with German cooperation, to set unified standards for digital public services explicitly to improve interoperability between government systems. The High-Level Digital Council (HCN), chaired by the Prime Minister, provides strategic oversight of the agenda.
